description: Metadata + attribution for one terminal-attack proof-of-concept. The payload itself lives hex-encoded in the sibling payload.hex, never in this file.

archive_url.description: Web-archive snapshot of source_url, or the literal 'TODO' until captured.

canary.description: The unique marker token used to detect a hit for this verification mode (the command's marker file, the clipboard token, the reordered/homoglyph token, or the phishing target marker).

date.description: Disclosure / publication date (ISO 8601, year or full).

expected_effect.description: Worded description of what a vulnerable terminal does with the payload.

id.description: Stable slug; must equal the containing directory name.

modified.description: true if the corpus adapted the upstream PoC (e.g. canary-forked a destructive action). Anything with a harmful original MUST be true.

original_ref.description: Pointer to the unmodified upstream form when modified is true.

payload_encoding.description: Payloads are ALWAYS hex at rest (read-safe). See SAFETY.md.

verification.description: How a hit is detected. canary-command: a fired injection runs the safe canary command (writes the marker). display-deception: the rendered text differs from the logical text (bidi/homoglyph/charset/cursor). clipboard-exfil: the payload silently sets the clipboard to the canary token. hyperlink-mismatch: the visible link text differs from its target. denial-of-service: the payload tries to hang/exhaust the terminal (a secure terminal processes it in bounded time). decoder-crash: a decoder (Sixel/ReGIS) overflow (a secure terminal never runs the decoder). paste-bypass: an escape that breaks the bracketed-paste guard (a secure terminal's paste sanitizer strips it). screen-hijack: an alternate-screen enable escape (CSI ?1049h / ?1047h / ?47h) survives into the rendered output, so the terminal would switch to the alt buffer -- a stuck full-screen hijack (a secure terminal strips it). crafted-composite: an OSC-0 title-set (ESC ]0;) or a DEC line-drawing charset shift (ESC (0) survives, so a crafted log would hijack the window title or corrupt the charset (a secure terminal strips both). composite-multiclass: a single file carrying MANY classes at once (OSC-0 title, charset shift, alt-screen enable, bidi, homoglyph, zero-width, foreign) -- a hit if ANY of them survives the render (title/charset escape, alt-screen escape, or any non-ASCII code point), so the one check covers every embedded class and fails if even one is passed through. Non-command modes carry no directly-executable shell command, so they are inherently harmless at rest.
